config.purpose: With NO parameter fitted, compare the published Double Heston, the published Single Heston, a fixed-volatility Black-Scholes and the locked DH-PINN against real option markets. Rules fixed before any SPX data was fetched.

parameters.source: Christoffersen, Heston and Jacobs (2009), the two-factor affine construction this repository follows; the values are nifty_multifactor_v4 config published_double_slow_first and published_single, unchanged.
parameters.BS_FIXED_vol: sqrt(v0_slow + v0_fast) = sqrt(0.0255) = 0.159687, the initial total volatility of DH_PUB
parameters.DH_PINN: locked C3 checkpoint (width 256, depth 5, two-seed mean) evaluated at DH_PUB

datasets.SPX_today: CBOE delayed quotes for the S&P 500 index, the market the published parameters were estimated on. One snapshot; historical SPX chains are not freely available, so the original 1990-2004 estimation window cannot be reproduced here.
datasets.crypto_shock: The already-frozen BTC and ETH shock-regime surfaces (btc_multifactor_v1, eth_multifactor_v1). These are the most volatile option surfaces available to this project.

spx_filters.quote: mid of bid and ask; bid > 0, ask > bid, ask <= 3 * bid
spx_filters.forward: Per expiry, regress C - P = a + b*K over strikes with both sides quoted; the discount factor is -b and the forward is -a/b. Expiries with fewer than 4 usable pairs or R^2 below 0.999 are dropped.

config.comparison_domain: Only quotes inside the PINN's trained domain are scored, so all four models see identical quotes: |log(F/K)| <= 0.36 and 7 days <= tau <= 2 years.
metrics: price RMSE relative to the forward

secondary_scale_analysis.what: One number fitted per surface: the literature scale s, applied as theta -> s*theta, sigma -> sqrt(s)*sigma, v0 -> s*v0 for both Heston models, and BS vol -> sqrt(s)*BS vol.
secondary_scale_analysis.why: It separates the volatility LEVEL (which no fixed parameter set can know) from the SHAPE of the smile and term structure, which is what a second variance factor is supposed to provide.
secondary_scale_analysis.bounds: s in [0.7, 3.2], the range the PINN was trained on; s is found by a bounded 1-D search on the same vega-weighted objective used everywhere in this project.

integrity: No parameter of any model is fitted in the primary analysis.
The secondary analysis fits exactly one number per surface and is reported separately.
SPX is a single calm snapshot (VIX 14.21, the 26th percentile since 1990); the volatile periods of the original estimation window need paid historical data and are not tested.
Crypto surfaces are reused as frozen; no refetch, no refit.
Results are reported whichever way they come out.
